endings.name: The Flake
endings.summary: The bark was over-tapped and over-carved. At the touch a plate gives and a district falls away. In the backyard a flake drops into the grass and nobody looks up; it lies face down, and its underside is not solid.
endings.cost: Twelve names go on the Roll. The flake's eaten underside clears Underhollow's name, too late for anyone who could be told; if the Pulse map was whole the plate was cleared first and the names are those who would not leave it.

endings.name: The War on the God
endings.summary: The Battlements lead, and read the Shadow as an enemy. The warriors climb the knuckle and Burr strikes. In the backyard someone picks out a splinter and goes inside. On the bark it is the greatest victory in history.
endings.cost: Two to four names on the Roll beside Burr's. The third tap never lands, so the question was never finished: Fenn's last entry is the next seventh day, already inked.

endings.name: The Edge of the World
endings.summary: The Scroll House leads and read the Shadow as a thing with a habit. The scholars stake its outline; Fenn draws the first map with an edge on it, and the city argues over whether it is heresy.
endings.cost: Fenn's map has an outer edge and an inner one, round the plates the Pulse lives behind. The heresy is double, and the Knot will not forgive the second edge.

endings.name: The Ring
endings.summary: The Knot leads, the Shadow is read as a hungry god, and the Great Offering is poured while the Trunk's Pulse is loud. The bark holds, and the second tap sounds like a drum. The hand goes and comes back, and when the light returns a band of colour circles the world. The people take it for a covenant. The pull-back shows a ribbon tied round the trunk and, over the fence, the stump the game has shown since spring. Last line (added): “The god had left them a ring. They counted it with the others.”
endings.cost: The kindest-looking ending is the one where the yard's verdict can be guessed: nothing on the bark knows what a ribbon on a trunk is for, and the game never says. The offering fed what is in the wood.

endings.name: The Shadow Passes
endings.summary: The story's own path: the priests chant, the warriors stand ready, the scholars record. The hand taps, presses a crack and goes away. The view pulls back to the backyard, and the moral closes the game.
endings.cost: Nothing is settled: the hand will come again, and the people never learn why it came. If the player found the Pulse, one image comes before the verbatim lines: at the feast, Fenn lays her ear on the wall.
